title: Vegan Holiday Treats: Mini Coconut Macaroons Measured with a Scoop
meta_description: Bake perfect, uniform vegan mini coconut macaroons every time. Learn how using a cookie dough scoop ensures professional results for your holiday treats.
html:
Holiday baking is all about the joy of sharing, but the cleanup and the stress of unevenly baked cookies can sometimes dampen the mood. If you are looking for a crowd-pleasing, plant-based dessert that looks as good as it tastes, these mini coconut macaroons are the answer. The secret to getting that professional, bakery-style look isn't a fancy oven—it's using a vegan mini coconut macaroons scoop to ensure every single treat is identical in size.

Why Uniformity Matters for Vegan Baking

Vegan baking often relies on binders like flax eggs, cornstarch, or coconut cream, which can behave differently than traditional eggs. When your treats vary in size, you run into a common frustration: the small ones burn while the large ones stay raw in the center.

By using a Cookie Dough Scoop, you eliminate the guesswork. When every macaroon is the exact same volume, they all reach the same internal temperature at the same time. This means you can pull the entire tray out of the oven at once, avoiding the "staggered bake" that often leads to overcooked edges.

Ingredients for Mini Vegan Coconut Macaroons

These treats are naturally gluten-free and dairy-free, making them a safe bet for guests with various dietary restrictions. You will need:

  • 3 cups shredded unsweetened coconut
  • 1/2 cup maple syrup or agave nectar
  • 1/4 cup melted coconut oil
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup almond flour (for structure)

Step-by-Step: Vegan Mini Coconut Macaroons Scoop Method

Start by preheating your oven to 325°F (165°C) and lining a baking sheet with parchment paper. In a large mixing bowl, combine the shredded coconut, almond flour, and salt. Stir in the melted coconut oil, maple syrup, and vanilla until the mixture is tacky and holds together when pressed.

Now comes the part where the tool makes the difference. Instead of using a tablespoon or your hands—which can get sticky and lead to inconsistent sizing—reach for your Cookie Dough Scoop. The spring-release mechanism allows you to drop a perfect mound of dough directly onto the parchment paper without the mixture clinging to the spoon.

Space the macaroons about an inch apart. Since these are "mini," a smaller scoop size is ideal to keep the baking time short and the texture chewy. Bake for 12-15 minutes, or just until the peaks turn a golden brown.

Pro Tips for the Perfect Vegan Mini Coconut Macaroons Scoop Result

To take these treats to the next level, try dipping the cooled bottoms in melted vegan dark chocolate. Because you used a Cookie Dough Scoop, the flat bottoms are uniform, meaning the chocolate will set in a neat, professional layer rather than pooling unevenly.

If you find your dough is too soft to hold its shape, pop the bowl in the fridge for 20 minutes before scooping. Chilling the coconut oil slightly firms up the mixture, making it even easier for the scoop to release the dough cleanly.

Cleaning and Maintaining Your Kitchen Tools

One of the best parts of using a spring-release scoop is that it minimizes the amount of dough smeared across your countertops. However, coconut oil and maple syrup can be sticky. To clean your Cookie Dough Scoop, rinse it immediately under warm water. For stubborn residue in the spring mechanism, a quick soak in soapy water will bring it back to perfect working order for your next batch of holiday cookies.

FAQ

Can I freeze these vegan macaroons?

Yes! Once completely cooled, store them in an airtight container in the freezer for up to three months. Thaw them in the fridge or enjoy them frozen for a refreshing, candy-like treat.

What if I don't have almond flour?

You can substitute almond flour with an equal amount of coconut flour, but be careful—coconut flour is much more absorbent. You may need to add an extra tablespoon of coconut oil to keep the dough from becoming too crumbly for the scoop.

Why did my macaroons spread too much?

This usually happens if the coconut oil was too hot when mixed or if the oven temperature was too low. Ensure your oven is fully preheated and consider chilling the scooped dough for a few minutes before baking to maintain those high, rounded peaks.
